D-F paradigm for raw LLMs (not D-R-H-F which needs fine-tuning)
High precision over recall (fewer hallucinated relations)
Chinchilla: more data × weak model > less data × strong model

title: AutoRE: Document-Level Relation Extraction with Large Language Models
abstract_snippet: Large Language Models have demonstrated remarkable progress in NLP. This paper introduces AutoRE, an end-to-end DocRE model that adopts a novel RE extraction paradigm named RHF (Relation-Head-Facts). Unlike existing approaches that embed relations directly into prompt templates as candidates, AutoRE does not assume known relation options. Using QLoRA, AutoRE achieves state-of-the-art results on Re-DocRED, surpassing TAG by 10.03% and 9.03% on dev and test sets respectively.

title: Attention Is All You Need
abstract_snippet: The dominant sequence transduction models are based on complex recurrent or convolutional neural networks that include an encoder and a decoder. The best performing models also connect the encoder and decoder through an attention mechanism. We propose a new simple network architecture, the Transformer, based solely on attention mechanisms, dispensing with recurrence and convolutions entirely.

relations.condition: as sole mechanism, replacing recurrence and convolution

relations.note: Transformers eventually replaced RNNs for most NLP
Retains encoder-decoder structure but replaces internals

title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding
abstract_snippet: We introduce a new language representation model called BERT, which stands for Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers. BERT is designed to pre-train deep bidirectional representations from unlabeled text by jointly conditioning on both left and right context in all layers. The pre-trained BERT model can be fine-tuned with just one additional output layer to create state-of-the-art models for a wide range of tasks.

relations.note: MLM is BERT's key innovation over autoregressive LMs

relations.condition: one additional output layer for task-specific models

title: Training Compute-Optimal Large Language Models (Chinchilla)
abstract_snippet: We investigate the optimal model size and number of tokens for training a transformer language model under a given compute budget. We find that current large language models are significantly undertrained. Our approach results in Chinchilla, a 70B parameter model that uses the same compute budget as Gopher (280B) but with 4x more training data.

relations.condition: same compute budget, 4x more data, 4x fewer parameters
relations.note: 70B params + more data > 280B params + less data
Scaling law: model size and data should scale together
Provides empirical evidence for compute-optimal scaling

title: ChatIE: Zero-Shot Information Extraction via Chatting with ChatGPT
abstract_snippet: This paper proposes ChatIE, a framework that transforms the zero-shot IE task into a multi-turn question-answering problem with ChatGPT. ChatIE decomposes complex IE tasks into simpler sub-tasks through multi-round dialogues, achieving 16.65% improvement over single-prompt baselines on RE tasks.

relations.note: Core idea: decompose IE into multi-round QA dialogue
Decomposition into sub-tasks is the key improvement

title: QLoRA: Efficient Finetuning of Quantized Language Models
abstract_snippet: We present QLoRA, an efficient finetuning approach that reduces memory usage enough to finetune a 65B parameter model on a single 48GB GPU while preserving full 16-bit finetuning task performance. QLoRA backpropagates gradients through a frozen, 4-bit quantized pretrained language model into Low Rank Adapters (LoRA).

relations.note: Key extension: frozen 4-bit base model + LoRA adapters
Dramatic memory reduction while preserving quality
